### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**36** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **29** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ca97d8c8e18c197f5e3808c03473710c0c035ce2` — the merge of head `e1305f7524b9172978bdc542dfc538bf153ee479` into base `14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ca97d8c8e18c197f5e3808c03473710c0c035ce2 && git checkout ca97d8c8e18c197f5e3808c03473710c0c035ce2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12 e1305f7524b9172978bdc542dfc538bf153ee479 && git checkout -B drift-repro 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12 && git merge --no-ff e1305f7524b9172978bdc542dfc538bf153ee479

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 14c67d446e577926460f3ed893e44cc32cbecb12` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d85dbe45f9f23db6758ffbb86fc1b031939f2724`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-start-hooks.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/grant-table-write-contract.dogfood.test.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/grant-permission-set-name.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/grant-holder-membership-refusal.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (destroy), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-permission-sets.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/bootstrap-platform-admin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/auto-org-admin-grant.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (insert and update hook dispatch), packages/objectql/src/engine-hook-dispatch.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-insert.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (getItem), packages/core/src/security/assemble-execution-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts, packages/core/src/security/security-catalog.ts, packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/position.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/identity/identity-assignment-body-writes.ts, packages/rest/src/batch-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/admin-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-membership-admission.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/demo-staff.ts, docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md (D10, D12 note). Prose faces (.changeset/sec-hardening-r6-agent-ceiling-grant.md, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx) are the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT; row 23f was read sentence by sentence here because the module header carries the same sentences.

Face: the paths decide no face (no published schema, no governed path); the committed changeset's line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the closed-pair spelling AGENTS.md step 3 names, so the face is narrowing and the tier is `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with ④. Rule under review: a person-to-permission-set assignment (`sys_user_permission_set`) refuses an MCP agent ceiling set at every write door, for every non-system writer. Full review (no prior at-tier record on any head; no `Contract-review-claim:` or hold on the PR).

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Accept set narrowed, correctly stated.** A non-system `insert` or `update` of `sys_user_permission_set` whose resulting row's `permission_set` is one of `MCP_AGENT_PERMISSION_SETS` (imported from `@objectstack/spec/ai`, never retyped) is refused. Insert judges the row as sent through the shared by-name reader `grantSetNameOf` (exact, trimmed); update judges the payload's `permission_set` when the key is present, else the stored row's. Held: `agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts` lines 141-160. Correct.
2. **Write doors into the table, enumerated independently.** The engine has three row-writing verbs (`insert`, `update`, `delete`; no upsert, restore or replace verb) and every direct `driver.*` write inside them runs after the before-hook chain (`engine.ts` insert: per-row `beforeInsert` precedes `driver.bulkCreate` / `driver.create`; update by id binds `hookContext.previous` at line 8669 before `driver.update`; predicate update dispatches `beforeUpdate` once per matched row with `previous` through `dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`; the ADR-0142 precondition path `updateByIdExpecting` is reached from `update()` after its hooks). HTTP doors all reach those two verbs: `POST /data/:object`, `PATCH /data/:object/:id`, `createMany`, `updateMany`, `POST /data/:object/batch`, `POST /batch`, `POST /data/:object/import`, `POST /data/:object/import/jobs`, `POST /data/:object/:id/clone` (engine insert) and `POST /data/import/jobs/:id/undo` (`updateData` under the caller's own context). Eight are pinned at HTTP in the dogfood block; clone and undo ride the same engine verbs and are covered by construction. The admin create-user grant (`admin-user-endpoints.ts` line 884) inserts under the calling administrator's context, so it is judged. Flow run-as-system and hook-action-body writes to both assignment tables are refused upstream (`flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts`, `IDENTITY_ASSIGNMENT_WRITE_OBJECTS`), so no non-system caller reaches a system write of this table through automation. Covered: every non-system door. Not judged, by the rule's own terms: `delete`, and every `isSystem` write. Correct for the rule as stated.
3. **isSystem stand-down.** The stand-down takes the shape of the siblings on this table (23c catalog name, 23d holder membership) and of the security middleware; its shape and priority are right. The module header's stand-down paragraph (lines 46-50) and row 23f's Get cell justify it with a property of the named system writers ("none of which names one") that the PR holds by construction for some of them but neither pins nor backs with a refusal for all of them. A claim is kept as narrow as its enforcement (AGENTS.md Prime Directive 10). **must-fix, see ④.** Detail is in the reviewer's local note, not here.
4. **Delete not judged.** Removal stays open to whoever the delegated-administration gate lets remove; pinned (unit "renamed to a person set, and can be deleted"). Correct.
5. **Envelope.** `validationFailure(message, [entry])` from `@objectstack/types`, the constructor both HTTP doors map to `400 VALIDATION_FAILED`; one `fields[]` entry `field: 'permission_set'`, `code: 'invalid_value'` typed to the closed `FieldErrorCode` catalog (ADR-0114; `reference_not_found` is the catalog sibling's member, the set exists here), `value`, `label`, a `constraint`. No new code (ADR-0112). Every refusal pin asserts `status`, `code` and `fields[0]` (`field`, `code`, `value`) through `resolveThrownHttpError` in the unit file and off the wire in the dogfood block; the two per-row-report doors assert `code` and `httpStatus` of the failed row; the two import doors assert `code` and `field` of the row report. Correct.
6. **Update keep-in-force semantic.** Judging the resulting row (payload set when present, stored set otherwise) is the right predicate: a new holder, a validity window or an echo on a stored ceiling assignment is refused; a rename away to a person set lands; a rename to a ceiling is refused by id and by predicate. Pinned per patch and by predicate. Correct, and stricter than the catalog sibling's echo rule for a reason the header states.
7. **Agent principal still gets its ceiling.** `assemble-execution-context.ts` lines 320-343 replace a user's resolved `permissions` with `agent.scopePermissions` for an OAuth client principal, and `security-plugin-permission-sets.ts` line 165 floors an agent at `mcp_agent_restricted` with no additive baseline; no assignment row is read for either. Pinned (unit "an agent principal holds its ceiling from its own context"). Unchanged by the diff. Correct.
8. **Hook ordering and registration.** Priority 35 sits between the catalog refusal (30, so an unknown name answers `reference_not_found` first) and the holder-membership refusal (40). The catalog lookup is an exact-name map (`registry.ts` `getItem`, `collection.get(name)`), so a case variant of a ceiling name never resolves to a set and is refused by the sibling, which is why the exact-match predicate is sufficient. Registration is idempotent through `unregisterHooksByPackage` before re-binding, warns and returns `false` on an engine with no hook registry; `registerStartHooks` calls it after the middleware, so the delegated-administration gate still refuses an organization administrator the same three sets on the boundary first (`delegated-admin-gate.ts` `ORGANIZATION_BOUNDARY_DENYLIST`). Correct. `SecurityPlugin.destroy()` unbinds only the catalog-name hooks (as it already did for the holder-membership sibling); a nit, not a finding.
9. **Tests are rule tests.** Unit: real `ObjectQL` over `driver-sql` on in-memory SQLite with the real `SecurityPlugin` started on it; 14 cases, every refusal identified by envelope and every store read back. Dogfood: a second top-level `describe` in the table's shared harness file (ruling 6583487846 shape), 8 cases on the booted showcase over HTTP, `beforeAll` asserting the catalog serves all three sets so the catalog sibling cannot answer first. Ablation in the body: guard replaced by a no-op through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, unit 7 failed / 7 passed with the red set being exactly the refusal pins; dogfood rebuilt and preflighted with `scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`, 5 failed / 3 passed, each door pin after the first also red alone; restored and green. Read-only here (`Local-runs: none`); the reading is the dev's, named to head `1b9179369a` for the ablation and `d85dbe45f9` for the reruns, and the code under test is identical between the two (the later commits are a merge of main and the docs row).
10. **Public surface.** No new symbol reaches the package entry (body: 0 hits on `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts` for the five names, positive control `SecurityPlugin` 24 each); `check:api-surface` is spec-only, so this is the right reading for a plugin. No widening; `no (narrowing)` is the correct arm.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/sec-hardening-r6-agent-ceiling-grant.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`, title with `!`, a BREAKING banner, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and the operator's fix (list query, delete or rename). AGENTS.md step 3: a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and disposition; `check-changeset-no-major` reads this exact pair as `none-clean`. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines at line start. Touched packages: `@objectstack/plugin-security` (published, changeset present), `@objectstack/dogfood` (`private: true`, none owed); `content/docs` is not a package. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay); no other login to name. PR is draft, base `main`, head repo equals base repo, `auto_merge` null (nothing to disarm on this FAIL), no governed path in the file list.
- Closing keywords: none in the body, correct for a security-seat PR with no card; the body's `[#26571]` sits only in the dogfood file's pre-existing header.
- Acceptance notes, each answered: (1) the per-row report doors (`updateMany`, per-object batch) carry `code` and `httpStatus` without `fields[]` — their existing report shape for every validation refusal, pinned as it stands, accepted; (2) stored assignments are not migrated — the changeset names the list query and both remedies, and the ADR-0087 marker is consistent with nothing authored changing, accepted; (3) `no (narrowing)` is the AGENTS.md closed-pair spelling and is what puts this PR on the narrowing face, accepted.
- `Skills-docs: none` is present and its reasoning holds: `skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md` "Assigning a permission set to a user" names the two existing value refusals and the authority rule, and no sentence there turns false. Should (not blocking): the section now lacks the third value refusal; a one-line follow-up docs card (skills/** is Tier H) would keep the skill complete.
- ADR-0090: the D12 note's own sentence "an agent ceiling is not a person's set" is what the diff implements for every writer; the same note's "assigns any set to anyone" for the tenant-level administrator now reads as any person's set. Should (not blocking, docs-only, Tier H): an amendment status line on ADR-0090 recording that reading.
- Test-budget: the touched dogfood file declares no `test-budget:` line and none is owed unless the timing window reads it above 10 s; it now boots the showcase twice (one per top-level block, a shape two other files already take). Question for the lane: if the window lists it, none of the three budget classes fits, so the remedy would be one shared boot, not a budget line.
- Dogfood battery: the body pins the full battery to `d85dbe45f9` (420 files, 3501 tests, no shard) and the earlier timeout to an unrelated file rerun green; the head's check-runs carry `Dogfood Regression Gate` success as well.
- CI at head `d85dbe45f9`: 54 check-runs, 40 success, 14 skipped (UI matrix and opt-in lanes), 0 failed, 0 in progress; all ten required contexts present with `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint UI`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`); the late `Check Changeset` rerun (job 127443493276) concluded success.
- Row 23f, sentence by sentence against the code: "a system writer is not judged" — held (`ctx.session.isSystem === true` returns on both hooks); "seed replay and the platform's own grant writers (the platform-admin promotion, the organization-admin reconcile, self-registration)" — those writers exist and write as the system; "none of which names one" — not backed for every named writer (see ① item 3 and ④); "nothing an agent relies on: an agent principal receives its ceiling from its consented scopes, never from a row" — held; "a non-system insert, or a non-system update whose resulting row names one, is refused 400 VALIDATION_FAILED / invalid_value at permission_set, for every caller, a platform administrator included" — held and pinned; "a delete is not judged" — held. The generated register rows name `#onInsert` and `#onUpdate` and `check:system-context-census` is green at head.

### ④ Design judgment

On the narrowing face, the narrowing is judged against the published spec on `main`. `packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts` declares the three sets as the agent's scope-derived ceiling ("pure capability ceilings"; `scopesToAgentPermissionSets` is the only producer), ADR-0090 D10 fixes that an agent principal's `permissions` are that ceiling (held in `assemble-execution-context.ts`, which replaces the user's resolved sets for an agent), and the D12 note states that an agent ceiling is not a person's set and already denylists the three for organization-level administrators (`delegated-admin-gate.ts`). The diff therefore takes no declared capability away at any consumer — the agent's ceiling path is untouched and pinned, removal stays open, every other set stays assignable — and makes the spec's own declaration real at the one table that could place a ceiling on a person. The envelope reuses the existing constructor and an ADR-0114 member; the hook shape, priority and idempotent binding match the two siblings on the same table; judging the resulting row on update is the right predicate for an assignment that must not be kept in force, and the engine binds `previous` on both update legs so the predicate is decidable per row. The design holds.

One must-fix, in the file under review:

- **must-fix** — `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts` lines 46-50 (the stand-down paragraph) and its prose twin, `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx` row 23f Get cell: the sentence "none of which names an agent ceiling set" is asserted of every named system writer and is not backed for each of them. Keep the claim as narrow as the enforcement (Prime Directive 10): either back the sentence for each named writer with a pin (and a refusal where the property is not fixed by construction), or restate the stand-down as the siblings 23c and 23d state theirs, with the Lose cell saying what the trust costs, and drop the clause from both places. Which remedy, and where it lands, is the seat's call under security-findings section 9.

Not blocking, recorded for the seat and the lane: the shoulds and the question in ③; `SecurityPlugin.destroy()` not unbinding this package (precedent: the holder-membership sibling); the new module carries no `scripts/adr-anchors/` entry (precedent: the catalog-name sibling has one, the holder-membership sibling does not). Other surfaces that distribute a permission set to a person were enumerated for the seat in the local note; they are outside this PR's stated rule and are not judged by this record.

The plugin-security module's code is byte-for-byte what `d85dbe45f9` carried; only its header comment moved, so items 1, 2 and 4 to 10 of ① on that record stand unchanged and are not re-argued here. The face is unchanged: no published schema and no governed path in the file list; the committed changeset's line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` decides the narrowing face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` with ④.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The must-fix of `d85dbe45f9` (① item 3 and ④ there): RESOLVED, by backing the claim.** The seat chose the first remedy. `assertAudienceConfig` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/audience-posture.ts` lines 315-323) now refuses a `selfRegistrationPermissionSet` in `MCP_AGENT_PERMISSION_SETS` (imported from `@objectstack/spec/ai`, never retyped), beside its `admin_full_access` refusal and through the same `fail()`, so the envelope is the one that refusal answers: an `Error` whose message is `[audience] invalid audience configuration: selfRegistrationPermissionSet must not be '...'` followed by the reason and the remedy ("Declare a permission set meant for people"). Both config doors call that validator on the whole declaration: the constructor (`auth-manager.ts` line 1654, so a stack config naming one stops the boot) and `applyConfigPatch` on the MERGED `next` (line 2132, so a settings patch that names one, alone or with its posture, is refused and the standing audience keeps ruling; `auth-plugin.ts` logs it at `error` with the validator's sentence). The self-registration grant writer reads only the standing audience (`auth-manager-membership-admission.ts` line 201 reads `audience.selfRegistrationPermissionSet` off `getAudience()`, which resolves `this.config.audience`, written only through those two doors), so "writes only the validated set" is held by construction. The narrowed stand-down paragraph (`agent-ceiling-grant-refusal.ts` lines 46-56) now says, writer by writer, what holds: fixed names in code for the promotion and the reconcile (held: `bootstrap-platform-admin.ts` writes `admin_full_access`; `auto-org-admin-grant.ts` writes an organization-admin set), the validated set for self-registration (held, above), and seeds "write the sets their stack declares, and nothing judges those against this rule" (held: `demo-staff.ts` lines 368-375 and seed replay write as the system; this is the deployment's own declaration, stated as unjudged rather than claimed safe). The claim is now exactly as wide as the enforcement.
2. **Row 23f at `e1305f7524`, sentence by sentence.** "a system writer is not judged" — held. "The platform-admin promotion and the organization-admin reconcile name their sets in code, and neither is a ceiling" — held. "the self-registration grant writes the configured `audience.selfRegistrationPermissionSet`, which the audience validation (`assertAudienceConfig`, plugin-auth) refuses when it names an agent ceiling set" — held and pinned. "Lose: seed replay and the development-only demo-staff seed write the sets their stack declares, unjudged, so a seed that names an agent ceiling set stores it" — held; it is the register's purpose to say what the skip costs, and this cell now does. "A non-system insert, or a non-system update whose resulting row names one, is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_value` at `permission_set`, for every caller, a platform administrator included; a delete is not judged (ADR-0090 D10)" — held and pinned, unchanged. The register rows for `#onInsert` / `#onUpdate` stand and `check:system-context-census` is green at head.
3. **The new pins are rule tests.** `audience-posture.test.ts`: `it.each(MCP_AGENT_PERMISSION_SETS)` under both self-registration postures, the throw matched by a regex anchored on the exact prefix `[audience] invalid audience configuration: selfRegistrationPermissionSet must not be '...' — it is the permission ceiling of an AI assistant connected over MCP` (the dots standing for the refused name), so a different refusal firing first cannot green it; control: `member_default` and `portal_user` stay declarable. `audience-posture-setting.test.ts`: the settings channel with `audience_posture: open` and the write ceiling as `audience_self_registration_permission_set`; asserts the standing `invite_only` keeps ruling, that the `error` log carries the REFUSED banner and the validator's own sentence naming the value.
